reason: Takizuka–Abe binary pairing reproduces the Landau–Fokker–Planck operator statistically; Langevin schemes are a separate, equivalent route, not the same algorithm.

fix.summary: Coulomb collisions are a Landau–Fokker–Planck diffusion in velocity space. PIC codes model them with Monte Carlo binary-collision pairing (Takizuka–Abe, Nanbu), which reproduces the operator statistically, or with equivalent Langevin stochastic kicks.

reason: Gauss's law alone doesn't capture PIC; the map should show the deposit–field solve–push cycle.

fix.map: \text{deposit }(\rho,\mathbf J)\to\text{Maxwell solve}\to m\,d\mathbf v/dt=q(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)

reason: Godunov/Riemann solvers came from gas dynamics and were extended to MHD; only constrained transport and divergence cleaning are MHD-native.

fix.summary: Numerical MHD must preserve ∇·B=0. Constrained transport and divergence cleaning were developed for this, while Godunov/Riemann solvers were carried over from gas dynamics. Together they underpin astrophysical MHD codes.

reason: Kramers–Kronig holds at fixed k, and a conducting plasma's ε has an ω=0 pole needing separate treatment; this is an application, not an identity.

fix.summary: Causality makes the plasma dielectric ε(k,ω) analytic in the upper half ω-plane at fixed k. So Kramers–Kronig links its reactive and dissipative (Landau) parts, once the free-carrier pole at ω=0 is subtracted.

reason: The DSA spectrum follows from elementary steady advection–diffusion matching across the shock; nothing essential comes from complex analysis or special functions.
Self-adjointness holds with the density-weighted (kinetic-energy) inner product, and only for static equilibria; flows give the non-self-adjoint Frieman–Rotenberg problem.

fix.summary: For static equilibria the MHD force operator is self-adjoint under the ρ-weighted inner product. So ω² is real and the spectrum has discrete parts plus Alfvén and slow continua. Equilibrium flows break this (Frieman–Rotenberg).

reason: Quasi-symmetry conserves canonical momentum only at guiding-centre order, and exact global quasi-symmetry is impossible (Garren–Boozer). This is an application of Noether, not an identity.

fix.summary: Quasi-symmetry makes |B| depend on ψ and Mθ−Nφ in Boozer coordinates. Guiding-centre motion then has a Noether-conserved canonical momentum and tokamak-like confinement. It holds only approximately (Garren–Boozer), and omnigeneity generalizes it.

reason: Cross-helicity is the Noether charge of fluid relabelling symmetry; magnetic helicity is a topological Casimir from frozen-in flux, not the same origin.

fix.summary: Ideal MHD conserves magnetic helicity, a topological Casimir of frozen-in flux, and cross-helicity, tied to fluid-relabelling symmetry (Noether). These invariants constrain reconnection, dynamos and turbulent cascades.

reason: The α-effect needs explicitly broken mirror symmetry (helical forcing); the genuine spontaneous breaking is the B→−B symmetry selected by the saturated dynamo.

fix.summary: MHD is invariant under B→−B, and a saturated dynamo spontaneously picks a polarity, so geodynamo reversals are hops between degenerate states. The α-effect instead needs explicitly broken mirror symmetry (helicity). Dynamo onset is a bifurcation.

reason: The closer counterpart is the thermal-QFT Debye (electric) mass, not Higgs/Meissner; the analogy to symmetry breaking is weak.

fix.summary: Debye screening gives a Yukawa potential with range λ_D, the classical form of the thermal-field-theory Debye mass. It only superficially resembles Meissner penetration depth or Higgs-phase gauge-boson range.

reason: Node b covers thermoelectrics too; Green–Kubo MD for lattice thermal conductivity is the main link and is established practice.

fix.summary: MD, including machine-learned potentials, computes ionic conductivity and diffusion in solid electrolytes. Through Green–Kubo or nonequilibrium methods it also gives lattice thermal conductivity for thermoelectric materials.

reason: Duplicates C0432 (same nodes, same MD–protein-folding link); merge any extra content there.
Dose engines use direct analog/condensed-history transport sampling (EGSnrc, Geant4, TOPAS), not Metropolis Markov-chain sampling.

fix.summary: Monte Carlo particle transport, analog for photons and condensed-history for charged particles (EGSnrc, Geant4, TOPAS), is the gold standard for dose calculation in photon and proton therapy. It tracks showers particle by particle.

reason: Fourier transforms belong to the differential-equations note's scope; no contour-integral or analyticity content is used here.
The Courant–Snyder invariant comes from Floquet theory of Hill's equation (Ermakov–Lewis invariant), not a Noether symmetry; Liouville comes from Hamiltonian flow.

fix.summary: Liouville's theorem conserves emittance under Hamiltonian beam transport. Floquet theory of Hill's equation gives the Courant–Snyder (Ermakov–Lewis) invariant for linear optics, and symplectic maps constrain the evolution. Radiation damping breaks both.

record.name: Lie-algebraic transfer maps (Dragt–Finn)
record.summary: Beamline maps are written as products of exponentials of Lie operators :f: acting on phase space. This factorization, with normal forms, gives symplectic nonlinear maps, resonance analysis and dynamic-aperture estimates.

record.name: δf PIC as Monte Carlo variance reduction
record.summary: Gyrokinetic δf particle-in-cell codes evolve only the perturbation weights, a control-variate form of importance sampling. Statistical noise scales as N^{-1/2}, and weight growth and noise accumulation limit long turbulence runs.

record.name: Bayesian integrated data analysis in fusion
record.summary: Fusion experiments combine heterogeneous diagnostics (Thomson, interferometry, magnetics) into joint Bayesian posteriors for profiles and equilibria. Forward models and nuisance parameters handle systematics.

record.name: Sedov–Taylor phase of supernova remnants
record.summary: Dimensional analysis with only E, ρ and t fixes the self-similar blast-wave radius R∝(Et²/ρ)^{1/5}. This describes the adiabatic phase of supernova-remnant shocks where particles are accelerated.

record.name: ML disruption prediction and RL plasma control
record.summary: Neural classifiers predict tokamak disruptions from diagnostic time series. Deep reinforcement learning has been used to control plasma shape and position on the coils, and cross-machine transfer remains open.

record.name: Tensor-train compression of Vlasov phase space
record.summary: Representing the 6D distribution function as a tensor train or MPS compresses phase-space grids. Low-rank structure enables Vlasov–Poisson solvers far below full-grid cost, with filamentation raising the rank.

record.name: Flux coordinates and magnetic-field geometry
record.summary: Stellarator design uses curvilinear flux coordinates (Boozer, Hamada), metric tensors and Jacobians to express |B| and field-line curvature. Geodesic curvature controls neoclassical drifts and the Mercier stability terms.
